az_dall_wall.blurb: Dall Wall is a bolted face in the Black Mountains outside Kingman, and the last of the walls you reach on the uphill trail in Golden Valley. It holds fifteen sport routes on basalt, from a single 5.7 and a 5.8 through a solid group of 5.9s and 5.10s, with five 5.11s at the top end. Lines are short to medium and the moves are pocket and edge climbing. The wall faces south, so it collects sun and stays comfortable in the cooler months but turns hot in summer. A good pick for a mid-grade day, with plenty of moderate options for newer leaders.

az_trad_rock.parking_note: Drive to the West Stronghold of Cochise Stronghold in the Dragoon Mountains: from Tucson take I-10 east to exit 303, south on AZ 80, left on Middlemarch Road, then left on Forest Road 687 and about two miles north. A final right turn leads to a circular parking area with the crag in view.
az_trad_rock.blurb: Trad Rock sits low among the granite domes of the West Stronghold in the Dragoon Mountains, one of three neighbouring rocks at the Isle of You. Despite the name it is a sport crag: fifteen bolted lines running from 5.6 up to 5.11, with the bulk in the 5.10 range and a handful of easier 5.8s and 5.9s on lower-angle slabs. The rock is generally good, though wasps and bees nest on the upper section. Early in the day the wall sits in shade, and the sun reaches it late morning. Bring a 60 m rope and a rack of quickdraws.

az_tool_shed_the.blurb: The Tool Shed is the main crag of Tanque Verde Canyon on Tucson's east side, reached from a roadside pull-out with a short walk of around ten minutes. It is a hard-leaning sport wall: fifteen bolted routes, nearly all of them 5.11 or 5.12, with one 5.10 and a single 5.13 bracketing the range. Routes are short, so expect steep, sustained climbing in compact lines. The cliff was once loose, and it has since cleaned up, though the lower part can still feel a little rough and the upper face is cleaner. Best suited to climbers who already lead 5.12.

az_lookout_mountain.blurb: Lookout Mountain is a small basalt crag in north-central Phoenix, handy for an after-work session. Most of the fifteen routes are short bolted sport lines, with a couple of trad climbs and one top-rope. Difficulty runs from easy fives through the 5.8 to 5.10 range, which holds the most routes, up to a few 5.11s and one 5.12. Belays below steep sections can need a spotter, and some of the rock is loose, so a helmet is worth wearing. The scree trail up to the cliff is loose, so it is better for experienced climbers than for a brand-new partner.

az_asu_main_campus.blurb: An urban buildering spot on the Tempe campus of Arizona State University, with most problems clustered in the central square. Fourteen of the fifteen listings are boulder problems on campus features such as stairwells, chimneys and building faces, and one is a roped trad line. Boulder grades start at the easiest end and run up past V7, though most sit between VB and V4. This is a city area with no natural rock, so the character depends on the structures themselves; some listings are historical and may no longer be current, so treat it as a curiosity rather than a destination.

az_chossmine_the.blurb: A steep limestone cliff on the rim of Jacks Canyon near Winslow, reached by a short trail dropping about a quarter mile from the canyon edge. All fifteen routes are bolted and hard: one 5.10, five 5.11s, four 5.12s and five at 5.13. The stone is loose and crumbly low down and noticeably better higher up, and some anchors are set in the poorer rock. The cliff faces the sun and heats up quickly, which makes it best on a cold winter day. It is a project-minded wall for strong sport climbers rather than a place for a first lead.

az_outer_rim.blurb: Outer Rim is a compact boulder area on the San Francisco Peaks above Flagstaff, at roughly 8,600 feet. It packs fifteen moderate problems into a small spot with a short walk in along a forest trail from the Viet Springs trailhead. Grades run from V0 to V5, with the largest share at V3 and V4, so it suits climbers looking for steady mid-grade circuits. The stone is sharp and rough on the skin, and the cool mountain air keeps summer days pleasant, especially morning and evening. Bring pads, and a spotter helps on some landings.

az_seven_samurai.blurb: Seven Samurai is a small slab-bouldering zone up Pima Canyon on the south side of Phoenix, a short scramble from the entrance of the canyon. There are fifteen problems, from very easy ones up to V7. The harder ones are friction-dependent slab lines, and they feel notably tougher when the sun is on the rock and temperatures climb above the 80s, so cooler days are far better. A handful of mellow problems nearby make it workable for mixed groups. Bring pads.

_conflicts.az_outer_rim: Stored rock is rhyolite; https://www.mountainproject.com/area/201061343/outer-rim says sharp andesite. Left unchanged.
